topStories.headline: 'Tenderloin Night Shift' Zombie Game Pulled After City Officials Call It Dehumanizing
topStories.dek: A developer built an AI-generated shooter game set on Tenderloin streets in a weekend — then took it down days later under pressure from Supervisor Bilal Mahmood and the City Attorney's office.
topStories.body:
A video game placing players in a nighttime Tenderloin where they shoot zombie-like figures was live for only a few days before its developer pulled it offline Friday, October 17, following a swift and unified condemnation from San Francisco city officials and neighborhood advocates. The game, titled 'Tenderloin Night Shift,' was created by developer Pierre-Louis Biojout using OpenAI's Codex over a single weekend. Among its enemy types were characters called 'the Folded,' a clear reference to the posture associated with opioid overdose. Local landmarks including a Waymo vehicle and scooters were rendered in the game's digital streetscape.

Supervisor Bilal Mahmood, who represents the Tenderloin as part of District 5, said the violent gameplay was 'dehumanizing and should never be normalized.' A spokesperson for the City Attorney's office called it 'abhorrent.' Jared Stearns of the Tenderloin Museum said the game was simply 'not representative of the Tenderloin.' Tenderloin resident William Duffy was blunt in his reaction, noting that crime rates in the neighborhood have actually fallen in recent months.

Biojout acknowledged that the way the game was promoted showed 'poor judgment,' and said that targeting people struggling with addiction or homelessness was never his intention. He refunded all advertisers and made a personal donation to Delancey Street, a rehabilitation nonprofit. The game had reportedly earned just over $300 during its brief run. Biojout's startup, NanoCorp, had been selling in-game ad space starting at $100 per week.

The episode touched a nerve partly because it arrives at a moment of genuine, if fragile, improvement in the Tenderloin. Sidewalk drug use has declined in 2026, several troubled blocks have been stabilized, and the neighborhood's SFPD district boundaries were redrawn in October to refocus patrol resources on the historic Tenderloin core. For residents and advocates who have spent years working toward that progress, a game that reduced their neighborhood to a shooting gallery landed as a provocation rather than satire.

topStories.headline: Board of Supervisors Unanimously Passes 'No Hidden Rent' Law, Making SF First in California to Require All-In Price Disclosures
topStories.dek: Landlords across San Francisco must now show renters the true total monthly cost — including amenity fees, trash charges, and other add-ons — upfront in listings and on the first page of leases.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Board of Supervisors voted unanimously on Tuesday, October 20, to approve the 'No Hidden Rent Act,' legislation introduced by District 5 Supervisor Bilal Mahmood that requires landlords to disclose every recurring fee in rental advertisements and lease agreements. The law is expected to make San Francisco the first city in California to mandate that a total estimated monthly cost be advertised alongside the base rent.

The measure responds to a pattern documented by the Urban Institute Initiative showing that hidden fees — covering items like pest control, trash concierge services, and amenity charges — can raise a tenant's actual monthly outlay by 10 to 30 percent above the advertised rent. Mahmood introduced the legislation in June, citing a citywide rent emergency declared by Mayor Daniel Lurie and a 26 percent year-over-year increase in asking rents driven in part by the AI industry's expansion.

Under the new law, landlords must list all mandatory and optional fees on the first page of any lease agreement and display a total estimated cost in online listings on sites such as Craigslist and Zillow. Tenants who discover undisclosed fees after signing may terminate their lease without penalty, and landlords may not evict renters for nonpayment of fees that were never properly disclosed.

The Tenderloin and Mid-Market neighborhoods, where many residents live in single-room occupancy hotels and older apartment buildings with complex fee structures, stand to be directly affected. Tenant advocacy groups including the Eviction Defense Collaborative worked with Mahmood's office in drafting the legislation.

topStories.headline: Mid-Market Arts Festival Draws a Crowd, but Questions Linger About Who the District Is Really For
topStories.dek: The inaugural Market Street Arts and Theater Festival brought thousands out on October 17, but a new SF Standard assessment published today finds the neighborhood's recovery still a work in progress.
topStories.body:
The inaugural Market Street Arts and Theater Festival, held on the evening of Saturday, October 17, drew crowds along six blocks of Mid-Market from Fifth Street to Van Ness Avenue, with more than 50 performances spread across 35 venues. The free event — anchored at UN Plaza and backed by $500,000 from a coalition of civic and private donors including crypto-billionaire Chris Larsen and the SF Downtown Development Corporation — was billed as the launch of a formal Market Street Arts and Theater District.

An assessment published this morning by the SF Standard found the festival charming but structurally uneven: most programming was held indoors, and some attendees found the event difficult to navigate. Still, festivalgoers who made their way through the corridor encountered aerial dance by Bandaloop above UN Plaza, a Broadway show-tune sing-along at the Orpheum, circus-theater acrobatics, and drag karaoke aboard a moving cable car hosted by D'Arcy Drollinger. City Hall lit its dome pink on the night in recognition of the event.

The broader district initiative, championed by Supervisor Bilal Mahmood and organized by the Mid-Market Business Association and Foundation under director Fernando Pujals, aims to activate vacant storefronts with pop-up performances and better lighting, with a focus initially on the 900 block of Market Street between Fifth and Sixth streets. A city-supported housing project at Market and Gough Streets is also set to provide below-market-rate units to working artists.

Not all Bay Area artists have embraced the effort. A contingent has called for a boycott of events funded by billionaire donors, citing concerns about outside money shaping what gets staged in a historically working-class neighborhood. For longtime Mid-Market stakeholders, the question is whether the momentum from one successful night can be sustained across the quieter weeks ahead.

events.title: SF Symphony: Hisaishi Conducts Hisaishi
events.location: Davies Symphony Hall, 201 Van Ness Ave., Civic Center
events.description: Composer-conductor Joe Hisaishi, whose scores include 12 Studio Ghibli films and Oscar-winning works by Hayao Miyazaki, leads the SF Symphony in a program of his own music — including the West Coast premiere of his Concerto for Orchestra, newly commissioned by the Symphony. The run opened Thursday; two performances remain this weekend.

events.title: Asian Art Museum: 'Vishnu's Cosmic Ocean' Opens
events.location: Asian Art Museum, 200 Larkin St., Civic Center
events.description: The nearly 20-foot West Mebon Reclining Vishnu — Southeast Asia's largest ancient bronze, on loan from Cambodia's National Museum — arrives at the Asian Art Museum for its only West Coast stop before returning home. The museum describes this as a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to see the sculpture at its full monumental scale; included with general admission. A public opening celebration takes place Sunday, October 25.

events.title: SF Symphony: Elim Chan Conducts Adams and Mendelssohn (Doctor Atomic Symphony)
events.location: Davies Symphony Hall, 201 Van Ness Ave., Civic Center
events.description: Music Director Designate Elim Chan leads the SF Symphony and Chorus in the orchestra's first-ever performances of John Adams's Doctor Atomic Symphony — an orchestral condensation of Adams's 2005 opera about J. Robert Oppenheimer — alongside Mendelssohn's Violin Concerto with French violinist Renaud Capuçon and choral works by Brahms and Arvo Pärt. An open rehearsal with an Inside Music Talk runs Thursday morning at 10 AM.

events.title: Asian Art Museum: Free First Sunday — Diwali Celebration
events.location: Asian Art Museum, 200 Larkin St., Civic Center
events.description: The museum marks Diwali on its monthly Free First Sunday, offering free general admission and special programming, alongside the newly opened 'Vishnu's Cosmic Ocean' exhibition and docent talks on the permanent collection.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack — Final Weeks of the 2026 Season
events.location: Fulton Street Plaza, 147 Fulton St., Civic Center
events.description: The free outdoor lunchtime concert series, now in its third season, wraps up its 2026 run with live local music and food trucks every Tuesday and Thursday through the end of the month at the plaza outside the Main Library. Admission is free.

moreNews.headline: SFPD Narcotics Unit Raids Smoke Shops Citywide; First Death From New Kratom-Derived Opioid Reported
moreNews.body:
San Francisco police announced on October 21 that Narcotics Unit officers served search warrants at multiple city smoke shops in September and October, seizing hundreds of items including kratom and 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) packets, suspected psilocybin, flavored tobacco, nitrous oxide canisters, and drug paraphernalia. The monthslong investigation focused primarily on shops in the Haight-Ashbury and Inner Richmond neighborhoods, though the SFPD noted the crackdown is citywide and being coordinated with the City Attorney's Office.

The raids coincided with a health alert issued by the SF Department of Public Health after the city's chief medical examiner detected MGM-15 — a potent semisynthetic opioid derived from kratom, sometimes called 'gas station heroin' — in a fatal overdose involving an adult who died in late September. Health officials said they believe the drug's effects can be reversed with naloxone (Narcan). The SFPD said it will continue targeting suspected criminal activity, illegal product sales, and sales to minors at smoke shops.

moreNews.headline: SFPD Tenderloin District Gets New, Tighter Boundaries — Effective October 1
moreNews.body: New patrol district boundaries took effect citywide at 6 a.m. on October 1, with the Tenderloin station's jurisdiction notably reshaped: Market Street and everything south of it reverts to Southern Station, while the Tenderloin district now extends north to Sutter Street and west to Van Ness Avenue, bringing Lower Polk and Lower Nob Hill under Tenderloin Station for the first time. The changes, developed by district captains, command staff, and community stakeholders as part of a mandatory 10-year boundary review, are intended to balance workloads, reduce response times, and concentrate Tenderloin Station's resources on the neighborhoods it was originally designed to serve.

restaurants.name: Brenda's French Soul Food
restaurants.description: The Bay Area's most-reviewed restaurant, serving New Orleans–inspired beignets, fried chicken, and Creole-accented plates from morning through dinner.

restaurants.name: Zuni Café
restaurants.description: James Beard Award–winning Market Street landmark celebrated for its wood-roasted chicken for two and impeccably sourced California-Italian menu.

restaurants.name: Absinthe Brasserie & Bar
restaurants.description: Hayes Valley brasserie serving upscale French and Northern Italian cuisine with a lively bar scene beloved by pre-symphony and pre-opera crowds.

restaurants.name: Chao Pescao
restaurants.description: Bright, colorful Latin Caribbean spot directly across from City Hall, known for arepas, empanadas, and tostones, open Tuesday through Saturday.

restaurants.name: Son & Garden
restaurants.type: New American brunch and dinner restaurant
restaurants.description: Lush, Thai-inflected New American restaurant from the Farmhouse Kitchen family, serving colorful brunch plates and a dinner menu in an Instagram-beloved setting.

restaurants.name: Saigon Sandwich
restaurants.description: Cash-only Tenderloin institution serving the city's most celebrated bánh mì, stuffed with roast pork, pâté, and fresh herbs, for over 40 years.

restaurants.name: Sungho
restaurants.description: Michelin Guide–recognized Tenderloin gem specializing in 24-hour-simmered gukbap (bone broth with rice), savory pancakes, and marinated raw crab.

restaurants.name: Tadu Ethiopian Kitchen
restaurants.description: Tenderloin original serving authentic injera-based Ethiopian dishes in an open-kitchen setting, open Wednesday through Monday for dinner.

restaurants.name: Golden Era Vegan Restaurant
restaurants.description: Long-running Civic Center plant-based kitchen serving a wide menu of Vietnamese and pan-Asian vegan comfort dishes, including pho, claypot rice, and banh xeo.

restaurants.name: Arsicault Bakery – Civic Center
restaurants.description: Civic Center outpost of the Bon Appétit–crowned best bakery in America, with a spacious open kitchen turning out croissants, kouign amanns, and café drinks daily.

restaurants.name: Villon
restaurants.description: Kelly Wearstler–designed dining room inside the San Francisco Proper Hotel, serving seed-oil-free California farm-to-table breakfasts and lunches daily.

restaurants.name: Charmaine's
restaurants.description: Stunning rooftop bar atop the San Francisco Proper Hotel, offering panoramic city views, curated cocktails, and an indoor-outdoor terrace designed by Kelly Wearstler.

restaurants.name: Sam's American Eatery
restaurants.description: Civic Center neighborhood staple steps from City Hall, drawing office workers and performing-arts visitors with a broad American and Korean-inflected menu.

restaurants.name: Bar Jamon
restaurants.description: Civic Center tapas bar open from late afternoon, popular with post-theater crowds from nearby Herbst and Davies Hall for its Iberian wines and cured meats.

restaurants.name: Cantoo Latin Asian Rotisserie
restaurants.description: Tenderloin standout blending Venezuelan and Chinese culinary traditions, earning a loyal following for its rotisserie meats and flavors that tell the story of its owners' heritage.

hotels.name: San Francisco Proper Hotel
hotels.description: Mid-Market landmark in a 1904 Beaux-Arts flatiron building, featuring 131 artfully designed rooms by Kelly Wearstler, Villon restaurant, and the rooftop Charmaine's bar.

hotels.name: Phoenix Hotel
hotels.description: Legendary Tenderloin rock-and-roll motor lodge that has hosted touring musicians from David Bowie to Kurt Cobain; under new ownership since early 2026 and committed to continuing its poolside concert traditions.

hotels.name: YOTEL San Francisco
hotels.description: Mid-Market hotel in the historic Grant Building offering 203 cleverly designed cabins with self-check-in kiosks, 24-hour gym, and co-working public areas.

hotels.name: Courtyard by Marriott San Francisco Downtown/Van Ness Ave
hotels.description: Full-service Marriott property on Van Ness Avenue in the Tenderloin, convenient to Civic Center, City Hall, and performing arts venues, with walkable restaurant access.

hotels.name: Tilden Hotel
hotels.description: Independently operated Tenderloin hotel on Taylor Street with a 24-hour gym, on-site restaurant and bar, and a welcoming staff noted by recent guests.

shops.name: Niebla
shops.description: Brand-new Tenderloin hybrid bookstore and café specializing in Latin American literature — about 60% of titles in Spanish — alongside espresso drinks and pan dulce; officially opened September 17, 2026 with city Storefront Opportunity Grant support.

shops.name: Readers Bookstore at the Main Library
shops.description: Beloved San Francisco Public Library gift shop and used bookstore inside the Main Library building, with a wide selection across subjects at accessible prices.

shops.name: Sheba
shops.type: Middle Eastern clothing and specialty goods shop
shops.description: New Tenderloin shop opened September 18, 2026 via city Storefront Opportunity Grant, stocking Middle Eastern clothing and prepackaged specialty food items.

shops.name: SF Arts Commission Gallery
shops.description: Free City-run gallery at 401 Van Ness Ave supporting Bay Area visual artists through rotating curated exhibitions, with additional displays at City Hall and the Veterans Building café.

artEntertainment.name: Asian Art Museum
artEntertainment.description: World-class museum in the historic Civic Center with more than 20,000 works spanning 6,000 years of Asian art; currently showing a Ha Chong-Hyun retrospective and Garuda in Bali through the fall.

artEntertainment.name: SFJAZZ Center
artEntertainment.description: The nation's first freestanding venue built for jazz, with the 700-seat Miner Auditorium and 100-seat Joe Henderson Lab; offering 350+ concerts this season including Hiromi and Lila Downs in October.

artEntertainment.name: War Memorial Opera House
artEntertainment.description: Magnificent 1932 Beaux-Arts hall, home to the San Francisco Opera and San Francisco Ballet, and a Civic Center architectural landmark where the United Nations Charter was drafted in 1945.

artEntertainment.name: Louise M. Davies Symphony Hall
artEntertainment.description: Home of the San Francisco Symphony, the modern glass-and-steel hall seats 2,743 and anchors the Civic Center performing arts campus alongside the Opera House and Herbst Theatre.

artEntertainment.name: Herbst Theatre
artEntertainment.description: Elegant 928-seat hall inside the War Memorial Veterans Building, hosting chamber concerts, lectures, and City Arts events in a space where the UN Charter was signed in 1945.

artEntertainment.name: Orpheum Theatre
artEntertainment.description: Ornate 2,200-seat 1926 Market Street theater operated by SHN, presenting major Broadway touring productions year-round in the heart of the Theater District.

artEntertainment.name: Golden Gate Theatre
artEntertainment.description: BroadwaySF's premier 2,300-seat Market Street venue presenting top-tier touring Broadway productions, sister house to the Orpheum.

artEntertainment.name: American Conservatory Theater (ACT)
artEntertainment.description: Award-winning San Francisco theater institution operating the Geary Theater and The Strand, known for innovative productions and actor training programs.

artEntertainment.name: The Warfield
artEntertainment.description: Beloved 2,300-capacity Market Street music hall presenting rock, pop, and indie acts in an ornate historic building at the center of a proposed Theater Arts District on Market Street.

artEntertainment.name: Great American Music Hall
artEntertainment.description: Ornate 1907 Tenderloin venue — with its original frescoes, columns, and balconies — presenting rock, folk, jazz, and indie acts for 700 guests; shows booked through November 2026.

artEntertainment.name: Bill Graham Civic Auditorium
artEntertainment.description: Massive 8,500-capacity Civic Center venue hosting major concerts, events, and conventions in an early-twentieth-century Beaux-Arts building directly on Civic Center Plaza.

gymsRecreation.name: FITNESS SF – Mid-Market
gymsRecreation.description: Largest gym in the Mid-Market area at 1 10th Street, with a private Performance Training Center featuring power racks and Olympic lifting platforms, plus a barnwood yoga studio and group fitness classes.

gymsRecreation.name: Orangetheory Fitness – Mid-Market
gymsRecreation.description: Science-backed group fitness studio near Civic Center offering treadmill, rowing, and weight-training interval classes, popular with neighborhood workers.

gymsRecreation.name: Federal Fitness Center
gymsRecreation.description: Well-equipped fitness center in the Civic Center federal building area, known for unlimited towels, friendly staff, and kettlebell classes — open to eligible members.

gymsRecreation.name: UN Plaza Fitness Court
gymsRecreation.description: SF Recreation and Park's free open-air Fitness Court at United Nations Plaza, featuring the 7-minute full-body workout system alongside free Zumba and yoga classes by Rae Studios.
gymsRecreation.address: United Nations Plaza, Market St & 7th St

gymsRecreation.name: Boeddeker Park
gymsRecreation.description: Renovated Tenderloin neighborhood park on Eddy Street featuring a children's play area, basketball courts, and a community garden, with periodic free outdoor concerts.

gymsRecreation.name: SunLight Yoga
gymsRecreation.description: Small Civic Center yoga studio offering gentle and adaptive classes valued by beginners and practitioners of all fitness levels.

gymsRecreation.name: Alchemy Springs
gymsRecreation.description: Post Street studio near the Tenderloin offering an eclectic mix of yoga, meditation, sound bath, and dance classes in a spiritually grounding environment.
